Somerville.narrative: Somerville's real estate market is operating at a fever pitch across all property types, with single families closing at a median of $1,245,000, condos at $995,000, and multi-families leading the pack at $1,398,000 — and with every segment hitting 100% or better on sale-to-list price, there is virtually no room to negotiate. The competition is fierce: roughly half of all multi-family sales closed above asking price, while condos and single families weren't far behind at 45% and 44% respectively, and with no measurable months of supply recorded across the board, inventory is essentially nonexistent. For sellers, conditions couldn't be more favorable — properly priced homes are generating multiple offers almost immediately, and multi-family owners in particular are seeing strong premiums that reflect Somerville's continued appeal as an investment and owner-occupant play. Buyers need to come fully prepared with pre-approvals, aggressive offer strategies, and the flexibility to waive contingencies, as hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $2,597,500 and selling at 103.3% of list price — with a remarkable 57.1% of homes closing above asking, signaling intense buyer competition in an extremely supply-constrained environment. The condo market, while more accessible at a $910,000 median, is no less competitive, with 73 units trading hands in the last 30 days at exactly list price and nearly 40% going over ask, reflecting strong demand from professionals and investors alike. Multi-family properties are trading at a $2,347,175 median with 98.2% of list price achieved and 25% selling above ask, offering slightly more negotiating room but still representing a landlord-friendly, high-barrier market. For sellers, near-zero months of supply across all property types means exceptional pricing power and quick exits; buyers, meanwhile, should expect to move fast, come in above ask, and have financing airtight before stepping foot through a door.

Medford.narrative: Medford's housing market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $872,525 and an eye-popping 73.3% of homes selling above asking price — averaging 104.5% of list price — signaling that buyers should expect to bring their strongest offers well above ask. Condos held steady at a $750,000 median with an even 100% sale-to-list ratio, while multi-families commanded a $1.1 million median despite a slightly softer 95.4% SP/LP ratio, suggesting some room for negotiation in that segment. With effectively zero months of supply across all three categories and 37 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is critically tight, giving sellers exceptional leverage and near-certain multiple-offer scenarios. Buyers entering Medford should be pre-approved, waiver-ready, and prepared to move fast, while sellers can expect swift sales and strong returns — particularly in the single-family segment where over-ask bidding wars are now the clear norm.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,010,750 and selling at a remarkable 110.3% of list price — meaning buyers are routinely paying $100,000 or more above asking, as evidenced by 83.3% of homes closing over list. Inventory is essentially nonexistent across all property types, creating an intensely competitive environment where even condos at a $385,000 median are closing above ask 66.7% of the time, and multi-families are fetching a median of $1,075,000 at 102.8% of list. For sellers, this is about as favorable a market as it gets — properly priced homes are generating multiple offers almost immediately, leaving significant money on the table for those who price strategically. Buyers, however, need to come prepared with strong pre-approvals, escalation clauses, and the flexibility to waive contingencies, as hesitation in this market almost certainly means losing out.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's single-family market is firing on all cylinders, with a median sale price of $1,305,000 and an impressive 104.0% sale-to-list ratio — meaning buyers are routinely bidding well above asking, as evidenced by 65.2% of homes selling over list price among the 23 closed sales in the past 30 days. Condos are nearly as competitive, with a median of $865,000 and 52.6% of units trading above asking, while multi-families came in at a $987,500 median though with a softer 94.4% SP/LP ratio and only 4 sales, suggesting that segment carries slightly more negotiating room. Inventory is essentially nonexistent across all property types, with months of supply so thin it barely registers — a clear signal that Arlington remains a severely supply-constrained market. For sellers, conditions are about as favorable as they get, and pricing aggressively at or just below market value to spark a bidding war remains the dominant strategy; buyers, meanwhile, should come prepared with pre-approval in hand, escalation clauses ready, and realistic expectations that waiving contingencies may be necessary to compete.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,600,000 and an eye-opening 66.7% of properties selling above asking price at an average of 102.8% of list price. Condos and multi-families are equally heated, with medians of $830,000 and $1,177,500 respectively, and both categories seeing half of all sales close over ask — condos actually leading the pack with a 104.0% sale-to-list ratio. With effectively zero months of supply across the board and only 19 total sales in the past 30 days, inventory is extraordinarily tight, signaling a severe imbalance between buyer demand and available homes. Sellers are in an enviable position to attract multiple offers and premium pricing, while buyers should be prepared to move quickly, waive contingencies strategically, and come in meaningfully above list price to have any chance of securing a home in this sought-after town.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's housing market remains firmly in seller's territory across all property types, with single-family homes commanding a median of $1,075,000 and selling at 101.7% of list price — nearly two-thirds of them closing above asking — signaling fierce competition among buyers in that segment. Condos are slightly more tempered at a $682,500 median and 99.5% SP/LP ratio, though still active with 14 units moved in the last 30 days and just over a third going above ask. Multi-families tell a different story at a $1,225,000 median with no homes selling over list price and only 3 sales in 30 days, suggesting that investor-buyers are negotiating harder as higher interest rates pressure the income math on those assets. With effectively zero months of supply reported across the board, sellers hold significant leverage — especially in the single-family space — while buyers should expect to move quickly, come in strong, and likely waive contingencies to compete.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is commanding serious attention, with a median sale price of $2,325,000 and homes closing at 98.1% of list price — 38.5% of them selling above asking — across 13 transactions in the past 30 days, all against a near-zero months supply that signals an extremely tight inventory environment. The condo segment is arguably even more competitive, with a median sale price of $816,500, a 101.1% sale-to-list ratio, and a striking 60% of units selling over asking price, suggesting that even the town's more accessible price points are drawing intense bidding activity. The lone multi-family sale at $1,060,000 closed right at list price with no over-ask activity, though one data point makes it difficult to draw broader conclusions for that segment. For buyers, Winchester across all property types demands pre-approval precision, fast decision-making, and a willingness to compete well above list — particularly in condos — while sellers are in an enviable position to price confidently and expect strong, often multiple offers in a market with virtually no competing inventory.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a $905,000 median sale price and a stunning 58.2% of homes selling above asking price at an average of 101.1% of list price — a clear signal that buyer demand is overwhelming available inventory. The condo market, Boston's most active segment with 338 sales in the past 30 days, shows slightly softer but still strong conditions at an $822,500 median with 27.8% of units trading over ask, offering buyers a comparatively better chance at securing a property without a bidding war. Multi-family properties are arguably the hottest investment play in the city, with a $1,200,000 median sale price and 42.6% of properties selling above list, reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand for income-producing assets. With effectively no measurable months of supply across all categories, sellers hold enormous leverage right now and should feel confident pricing assertively, while buyers must come prepared with strong pre-approvals, competitive escalation clauses, and minimal contingencies to have any real shot at success in this market.
